verbs.title: Read the grid
verbs.description: Read a building's grid: every grid line's id (gx0, gx1, … along x; gy0, gy1, … along y) and its position in metres in the building's own frame, plus the structural system, the material, the number of girders and the building's rotation in degrees. Opens a fresh copy of the building; takes about 10 to 40 seconds. Changes nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Hospital" or "HospitalGarage".

verbs.title: Try shifting a grid line
verbs.description: Shift one grid line, and every later line on the same axis, by a distance in metres (positive = towards higher positions). Only the bay just before that line changes width; the rest of the building travels with it. The app makes the change, checks it (overlaps, beam spans against their limit, doors and windows against their walls) and returns its report: what changed, each check before and after, and what was not checked. If the change adds new problems the app undoes it and returns stopped_by_gate with the reason. Opens a fresh copy each time; nothing is saved.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, as in bim_lines.

inputs.name: line
inputs.description: The grid line to shift, e.g. "gx6".

inputs.name: move
inputs.description: The distance in metres, e.g. 1.824. Negative moves towards lower positions.

verbs.title: Count elements
verbs.description: Open a building in the Viewer and count its elements, the same answer the Viewer's Find panel gives for "Find element count by discipline" (or by storey). Returns the total and the count per group, plus the Viewer's own log line for the same answer. Opens a fresh headless copy of the Viewer on the CPU; takes about 20 to 90 seconds. Changes and saves nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex" or "Clinic". An unknown name is an error.

inputs.name: by
inputs.description: What to count by: "discipline" (the default, e.g. ARC, MEP) or "storey" (floor level).

verbs.title: List clashes between two disciplines
verbs.description: Open a building in the Viewer and list the clashes between two disciplines, the same answer the Viewer's Find panel gives for "Find clashes between A and B": how many element boxes overlap at the rule's tolerance (in metres), how many of those are true clashes after the shape tests, and the first 20 rows with the overlap in metres. A pair with no clash rule is an error, not zero. Opens a fresh headless copy of the Viewer on the CPU; takes about 20 to 120 seconds. Changes and saves nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Clinic". An unknown name is an error.

inputs.name: discA
inputs.description: First discipline code, e.g. "ARC" (architecture), "STR", "MEP".

inputs.name: discB
inputs.description: Second discipline code, e.g. "MEP". Order does not matter.

returns.shape: viewer_verbs JSON as viewer.counts, plus cols, rowsTotal, rows

verbs.title: Film path visibility
verbs.description: For a Viewer database that holds drawn services, report per film-camera band how many drawn lines and markers fall inside the film camera's view. Opens a headless copy of the Viewer on the CPU. Reads only: no bake, no GPU, nothing written. A database with no drawn services, or a path no sample of which lies on a band, is inconclusive, not zero.

inputs.name: db
inputs.description: Path to the Viewer database (.db) to judge.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Optional override file with the cinema_path bands to judge instead of the database's own.

returns.shape: film_path_vis --json {verdict SEES|BLIND|INCONCLUSIVE, per, totalLines, totalMarkers, log}

verbs.title: Schedule state at a day
verbs.description: The 4D state of a building at one day: how many elements are placed, being installed (frontier) or not yet built, which tasks are done, active or pending, the count per phase, and the schedule run's own log. Read from the persisted run of the shipped 4D pipeline (about 1 second); when no run matches the current schedule code and building database, the pipeline is run once and persisted, which takes up to a few minutes for a large building. Judged on the played layer, the one the film and the Time Machine scrubber reveal. A building with no schedule is inconclusive, not zero. Changes and saves nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex" or "Hospital". An unknown name is an error.

inputs.name: day
inputs.description: Whole days from the project start (day 0 is 2026-01-01); the state is taken at the start of that day. A day past the end shows everything placed.

verbs.title: Schedule engine against its reference
verbs.description: Run the schedule engine on a building's real elements and compare it, element by element, with the reference calculation (the gate's schedule followed by the critical-path solve) on the same data; then check that no element floats in mid-air on the solved times. Returns each row of the comparison (elements checked, mismatches, missing, largest difference in milliseconds, floating counts) and the engines' own log. A comparison that judged no element is inconclusive, never a pass. Takes under a minute for a small building and a few minutes for a large one. Changes and saves nothing.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex" or "Hospital". An unknown name is an error.

inputs.name: shift_hours
inputs.description: Hours in a working shift for the schedule (default 24, the comparison's own default).

verbs.title: Widen a bay to a target width
verbs.description: Composed verb: read the grid, compute how far the line "to" must move so the bay from "from" to "to" has the target width (in metres), and try that shift, with the same checks and the same stop as modeller.try_shift. Nothing is saved.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name.

inputs.name: from
inputs.description: The grid line at the start of the bay.

inputs.name: to
inputs.description: The grid line at the end of the bay; this line and every later one on its axis moves.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: The bay width wanted, in metres.

returns.shape: the envelopes of its lines, in answer.lines; the last is modeller.try_shift's

verbs.title: What the walker would place
verbs.description: A dry run of the Modeller's discipline walker on a building: what it would place for one discipline, as counts (total, by class, by host state, by how each position was derived, provisional, plan-only), with the walker's own log lines. The model is the one the Modeller's Open list names for the building; the rules are the ones the building's class uses (a residential building walks the residential rules). Nothing is placed, committed or saved: the model file is byte-identical afterwards. A walk that places nothing is inconclusive with the walker's reason, not zero. An unknown building or discipline is an error naming the legal ones.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name as the Modeller's Open list names it, e.g. "Duplex" or "Hospital". An unknown name is an error that lists the names.

inputs.name: discipline
inputs.description: The discipline to walk, e.g. "FP" (fire protection), "ELEC", "PLB", "ACMV". Must be one the building's rules hold; otherwise an error lists them.

verbs.title: Describe an object kind
verbs.description: Reflection. Given a kind (and optionally one record), return what the model's own dictionary says about it: each property (name, type, mandatory, updateable, key, list values, min and max), the child tabs below it, and the generic methods that are legal for it (read, update, attach, history). Reads only dictionary rows; no data row is opened. An unknown kind is an error naming it. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: Optional. A record's UU; the answer then also names how its child tabs link to it.

verbs.title: Read an object
verbs.description: Read one record of a registered kind by its UU key, with the rows of its single-row child tabs (for an element, its transform). Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

verbs.title: History of an object
verbs.description: The change-log rows legacy iDempiere would have written for one record, derived from the op-log of edits made through the object engine (column, old value, new value, event). Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

verbs.title: Change one property of an object
verbs.description: Change one property of a record of a registered kind. The dictionary decides whether it may: the property must exist and be updateable, a list value must be on its list, a number must be a number, a mandatory property may not be emptied. A refusal says which rule. The change is written as an op to the op-log, not into the model file.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: The property to change, as describe lists it, e.g. "element_name".

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The new value, as text.

verbs.title: Attach a file or note to an object
verbs.description: Attach a file (or a text note) to a record of a registered kind, the way the ERP window's Attachment button does: one attachment row per record, keyed by the record's UU. Written as an op to the op-log, not into the model file. A kind whose key is neither an _ID nor a _UU column cannot have attachments.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: uu
inputs.description: The record's UU key (for an element, its IFC guid).

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: Path of the file to attach.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: A text note to attach, when no file is given.

verbs.title: Count the records of a kind
verbs.description: How many records of a kind a model holds, as its own dictionary names the kind, e.g. how many rooms. Further column=value inputs narrow the count; each column is checked against the kind's properties, and an unknown column is an error that names it. The answer also gives the population (the kind's records with no filter). A kind with no record at all is inconclusive, not zero. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Room" or "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it must equal

verbs.title: List records of a kind
verbs.description: List the records of a kind as rows. Columns, filters and the sort are checked against the dictionary: an unknown column is an error that names the kind's properties. Shows at most 50 rows unless limit says otherwise (up to 1000); the answer always carries the total, so a short list is never mistaken for the whole. Nothing is changed. Add column=value to filter (several allowed).

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Room" or "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Optional: the columns to show, comma separated, e.g. DocumentNo,DocStatus. Default: the key, the number or name, and DocStatus where the kind has one.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.description: Optional: a column to sort by; a leading - sorts descending.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Optional: how many rows to show (1 to 1000, default 50).

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Optional: skip this many rows (to page through a long kind).

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it must equal (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Add up a column
verbs.description: The exact sum of one number column over the records of a kind (all of them, or those matching column=value filters). Decimals are added exactly, never as floating point. An empty kind is inconclusive, never a plain 0. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Room" or "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: The number column to add up (an amount, quantity, number or whole-number property).

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it must equal (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Count by a column
verbs.description: How many records of a kind carry each value of one column, most common first (all records, or those matching column=value filters). The total is always given. An empty kind is inconclusive. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: building
inputs.description: The building name, e.g. "Duplex". Its model must carry its own dictionary (a patch with the object layer).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of object, as the model's dictionary names it, e.g. "Room" or "Element". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the model registers.

inputs.name: by
inputs.description: The column to group by.

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it must equal (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Run a witness and read its verdict
verbs.description: Runs the witness named witness_<name>.js from this tree, keeps its whole log under the cache, and answers the witness's own verdict line (PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE) with the pass, fail and inconclusive counts and the lines that failed. A witness that prints no verdict line is an error: an exit code is not evidence. The log path is in the answer.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The witness name without witness_ and .js, e.g. "erp_new". More than one match is refused naming both.

verbs.title: Read the last recorded witness run
verbs.description: Answers the last run of a witness that witness.run recorded, without running it again. Nothing recorded is refused with the instruction to run it first.

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: The witness name without witness_ and .js.

returns.shape: ops_cli JSON as witness.run, plus recorded:true

verbs.title: Is the legacy test stack up
verbs.description: Checks the legacy iDempiere test stack the twin is compared against: the docker Postgres container and the pilot web UI. Answers UP, PARTIAL or DOWN with each part's state, and the commands that start it when it is not up. Reads only; it starts nothing.

verbs.title: Read rows of a legacy table
verbs.description: Reads rows from a table of the legacy iDempiere database (read only). The table and every column are checked against the legacy dictionary, so a wrong name is refused and the real columns are listed. Give column=value to narrow. At most 50 rows unless limit says otherwise (up to 1000); total is always given. Legacy not reachable answers inconclusive.

inputs.name: table
inputs.description: The legacy table, e.g. "c_order".

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Comma-separated columns to show (default: the identifying ones).

inputs.name: sort
inputs.description: A column to sort by; a leading - sorts descending.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: How many rows to show, 1 to 1000 (default 50).

rest.what: column=value, a column of the table and the value it must have (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Who fills a column: twin and legacy side by side
verbs.description: Looks a column up in the twin's dictionary and the legacy dictionary and answers, for each: the column default, the validation rule, the field default, and the login default (the row of the referenced table with IsDefault=Y, which iDempiere puts in the context at login). Says what fills it and whether the two sides agree. Legacy not reachable gives the twin side only, marked not checked.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The table or window kind, e.g. "Order" or "C_Order".

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: The column, e.g. "C_ConversionType_ID".

verbs.title: Compare one record on the twin and on legacy
verbs.description: Reads one record by its Document No on the twin and the matching record on legacy and compares them cell for cell. Each differing cell is classed DIFF, ONLY-TWIN, ONLY-LEGACY, or NULL-VS-DEFAULT (legacy empty where the twin holds 0, N or empty: say nothing about the cause). Ids, audit stamps and dates are skipped and counted. An ambiguous legacy number is refused naming the ids; legacy=<number> picks it.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, e.g. "Order".

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The Document No on the twin.

inputs.name: legacy
inputs.description: The Document No on legacy when it differs from the twin's.

calls.who: the twin and the legacy database

verbs.title: Find a name in the iDempiere source
verbs.description: Finds the lines of the legacy iDempiere Java source that contain a name (a column, a class, a method) and answers file, line and the line's text, so a claim about legacy behaviour can cite its source. in=<text> keeps only files whose path contains it (e.g. callout). At most 25 lines unless limit says otherwise; the total is always given. No match is inconclusive, not zero.

inputs.name: symbol
inputs.description: A name: letters, digits, _ and . (e.g. InvoiceRule or CalloutOrder.docType).

inputs.name: in
inputs.description: Keep only files whose path contains this text.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: How many lines to show, 1 to 200 (default 25).

verbs.title: Make the 2Pack zip from a data-model workbook
verbs.description: Reads an ERP data-model workbook (one sheet per dictionary table: table, columns, reference lists, window, tabs, menu, process rows with class names only, plus a Plugin sheet) and writes the metadata-only 2Pack zip a legacy iDempiere applies. Written once per version: the same version with the same rows answers unchanged, the same version with different rows is refused (a released pack is immutable; bump the version). The answer gives the zip's path, its sha256, the rows per dictionary table and the process class names the pack points at. With java= the Java model classes of the tables the workbook creates are written too; the rules (document actions, process bodies) stay hand-written. A person runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms.

inputs.name: book
inputs.description: The workbook, a .xlsx path inside this tree or the working folder (no .. and no absolute path).

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: The pack version, x.y.z.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Folder to write META-INF/2Pack_<version>.zip under (default: the door's cache).

inputs.name: java
inputs.description: Folder to write the generated Java model classes under (optional).

inputs.name: package
inputs.description: Java package of those classes (default org.kernel.bim.model).

verbs.title: Start the shared docker Postgres for the legacy test stack
verbs.description: Starts the shared docker Postgres container the legacy test instance and the pilot read their databases from, when it is not running, and waits until it accepts connections. When it is already running it says so and starts nothing. It never starts or stops the instance or the pilot. Docker not reachable is inconclusive; a missing container is refused naming it. A person runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms.

verbs.title: Refresh the legacy test instance from the base seed
verbs.description: Rebuilds the local legacy iDempiere TEST instance (database idempiere_bimdoc, ports 8108 and 8464) from the base seed so every state traces from base: stops it, drops and recreates the database, imports the seed, applies the migration scripts newer than the seed, installs the plugin bundle, starts it, waits for the 2Pack to be installed and reads the rows back. About two minutes. It names the database it writes and refuses the pilot's databases; the instance, the database and the scripts are fixed, nothing is taken from the caller. A person runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms.

verbs.title: Run the in-server witness on the legacy test instance
verbs.description: Sends the witness command to the running legacy test instance over its OSGi console. The witness creates its rows in one transaction and rolls it back. Answers PASS or FAIL with the counts and the failing lines, or INCONCLUSIVE when the instance is not running. The log is kept.

verbs.title: Check a workbook's rows in the legacy test database
verbs.description: Reads every row of a data-model workbook back from the legacy test database by SQL (tables, physical tables, columns, windows, tabs, menu, processes with their class names, references) and answers how many of each were found. With version=<x.y.z> it also compares the installed plugin's 2Pack with the pack made from the workbook (build/legacy_plugin) and says plainly when they differ. Database not reachable is inconclusive.

inputs.name: book
inputs.description: The workbook, a .xlsx path inside this tree.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: The pack version to compare, x.y.z.

verbs.title: Put a data-model plugin on the legacy test instance and check it there
verbs.description: The whole route for a plugin on a real legacy iDempiere, one line: start the docker Postgres if it is not running, make the 2Pack from the workbook, refresh the local legacy test instance from the base seed with the plugin bundle installed, read every row of the workbook back from the test database, and run the in-server witness. Each step is its own line and the first line that is not ok stops it. The refresh installs the plugin bundle as committed, so the check says when the installed pack is not the one just made from the workbook. About three minutes. A person runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms.

inputs.name: book
inputs.description: The workbook, a .xlsx path inside this tree.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: The pack version, x.y.z.

returns.shape: the envelopes of its lines, in answer.lines; the last is legacy.witness's

verbs.title: Find a document
verbs.description: Find a document by its number, the way a window's Find does (DocumentNo, else Name or Value). Returns every match with its key, DocStatus and DocAction. Nothing is changed. Kinds: any document table of the dictionary (34).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of document, as the dictionary names it (an AD_Table with a DocAction column), e.g. "Order". 34 kinds exist; an unknown kind or a table that is not a document is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The document number (DocumentNo) as shown in the window; if two documents carry it, name one with id.

verbs.title: What can be done to a document
verbs.description: The legal document actions for this document in its current state, from the engine's own list (DocumentEngine.getValidActions), then narrowed by the role's Document Action Access when a role is given. Nothing is changed. The reply's `next` carries the same list.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of document, as the dictionary names it (an AD_Table with a DocAction column), e.g. "Order". 34 kinds exist; an unknown kind or a table that is not a document is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: The document's key (its _ID), as erp.find returns it.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The document number (DocumentNo) as shown in the window; if two documents carry it, name one with id.

inputs.name: role
inputs.description: Optional: an AD_Role id. The answer is what that role is OFFERED (Document Action Access, as the window's action list does); without it, the engine's own legal set.

verbs.title: Complete a document
verbs.description: Generate documents and complete transaction. Runs DocAction CO through the ERP engine (DocumentEngine.processIt) on the named document, with the books it posts. Offered for: Order (C_Order) (each compared with legacy iDempiere in the parallel run, evidence common/door/tests/logs/a5_erp_complete_parity.log). A person at the terminal runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms. A refusal says which rule.

verbs.title: Describe a kind of ERP record
verbs.description: Reflection over the application dictionary: the properties of a kind (name, type, mandatory, updateable, list values), its child tabs and the generic methods it supports, read only from the AD rows. Works for any AD table, a document or not. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: An AD table, by its name or table name, e.g. "Order" or "C_BPartner". An unknown kind is an error that lists the kinds the dictionary registers.

verbs.title: Read an ERP record
verbs.description: Read one record of any AD table by its key or by its number (DocumentNo, else Name or Value, as erp.find), with the rows of its single-row child tabs. Nothing is changed. The record shown includes what earlier verbs (erp.complete) wrote to the ERP op-log. A number that several records carry is refused naming their ids.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (an AD table), e.g.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: The record's key value (its _ID). Give this or number.

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The record's number as the window shows it (DocumentNo, else Name or Value); if several records carry it, name one with id.

verbs.title: List records
verbs.description: List the records of a kind as rows. Columns, filters and the sort are checked against the dictionary: an unknown column is an error that names the kind's properties. Shows at most 50 rows unless limit says otherwise (up to 1000); the answer always carries the total, so a short list is never mistaken for the whole. Nothing is changed. Add column=value to filter (several allowed).

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (any AD table), e.g. "Order". An unknown kind is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Optional: the columns to show, comma separated, e.g. DocumentNo,DocStatus. Default: the key, the number or name, and DocStatus where the kind has one.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.description: Optional: a column to sort by; a leading - sorts descending.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.description: Optional: how many rows to show (1 to 1000, default 50).

inputs.name: offset
inputs.description: Optional: skip this many rows (to page through a long kind).

inputs.name: names
inputs.description: Optional: Y shows each lookup column as the name of the record it points at (as the window's grid does, and as mis.load reads it) instead of its key.

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it must equal (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Add up a column
verbs.description: The exact sum of one number column over the records of a kind (all of them, or those matching column=value filters). Decimals are added exactly, never as floating point. An empty kind is inconclusive, never a plain 0. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (any AD table), e.g. "Order". An unknown kind is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: The number column to add up (an amount, quantity, number or whole-number property).

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it must equal (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Count by a column
verbs.description: How many records of a kind carry each value of one column, most common first (all records, or those matching column=value filters). The total is always given. An empty kind is inconclusive. Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (any AD table), e.g. "Order". An unknown kind is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: by
inputs.description: The column to group by.

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it must equal (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Create a record
verbs.description: Create a record of any kind the way its window does: the window's own defaults and callouts fill what you leave out (location, price list, warehouse, payment term, price, tax, line amount), your columns are set one by one as edits, mandatory columns are checked, and the Document No comes from the sequence. Give a column as column=value. A column that holds another record may be given by its number or name (a partner by name, a product by name); two matches are refused naming both. A line names its document by number: order=50000. A Sales or Purchase document needs issotrx=Y or issotrx=N. The answer starts with the new record's number. A person runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms. A refusal says which column is missing.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (any AD table), e.g. "Order". An unknown kind is refused naming the reason.

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it takes (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Change a record
verbs.description: Change columns of one record the way its window does: each column=value is an edit in the order given, its callouts fire (a partner change moves location, price list, terms), a column the window would not let a person edit is refused naming the rule (read-only, not updateable, the link column, a processed record), a mandatory column left empty is refused, and the model layer saves the changed columns as one group. Nothing is written when anything is refused. Giving the current values changes nothing and says NO-OP. A column that holds a record may be given as its number or name; the value <null> clears a column.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (any AD table), e.g. "Order". An unknown kind is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: The record's key (its _ID).

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The record's number (DocumentNo, else Value, else Name), as mis.read finds it; if two carry it, name one with id.

rest.what: column=value, a property of the kind and the value it takes (give as many as you like)

verbs.title: Delete a record
verbs.description: Delete one record the way the window's Delete does: refused when the tab is read-only or the table not deleteable, when the record is Processed (completed documents are voided or reversed instead), when a model or validator vetoes, or when other records depend on it; the rows its dictionary rule cascades to go with it. The refusal carries the engine's own reason and writes nothing.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (any AD table), e.g. "Order". An unknown kind is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: The record's key (its _ID).

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The record's number (DocumentNo, else Value, else Name), as mis.read finds it; if two carry it, name one with id.

verbs.title: Load records from a CSV
verbs.description: Load many records of one kind from a .csv file through the Migrate Excel Data process, as it is: the first line is the AD column names, one line per record, each lookup column (_ID) given as the name of the record it points at (or Column>Alt for another identifier), every cell read as text (007 stays 007), each line saved through the model layer so defaults and checks run. The loader is ALL OR NOTHING: with dry=Y (the default) nothing is loaded, the answer says how many lines are fine and lists each rejected line with its reason, and writes <file>.rejected.csv (the bad lines and why) and <file>.ok.csv (the good ones); with dry=N it loads, and refuses if any line is rejected, so load the .ok.csv. Updating existing records is mis.update.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, as the dictionary names it (any AD table), e.g. "Order". An unknown kind is refused naming the reason.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: The path of a .csv file on this computer.

inputs.name: dry
inputs.description: Y (default): check only, write nothing but the .rejected.csv and .ok.csv beside the file. N: load.

verbs.title: Who fills a column: twin and legacy side by side (old name of mis.column)
verbs.description: Looks a column up in the twin's dictionary and the legacy dictionary and answers, for each: the column default, the validation rule, the field default, and the login default (the row of the referenced table with IsDefault=Y, which iDempiere puts in the context at login). Says what fills it and whether the two sides agree. Legacy not reachable gives the twin side only, marked not checked.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The table or window kind, e.g. "Order" or "C_Order".

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: The column, e.g. "C_ConversionType_ID".

verbs.title: Compare one record on the twin and on legacy (old name of legacy.compare)
verbs.description: Reads one record by its Document No on the twin and the matching record on legacy and compares them cell for cell. Each differing cell is classed DIFF, ONLY-TWIN, ONLY-LEGACY, or NULL-VS-DEFAULT (legacy empty where the twin holds 0, N or empty: say nothing about the cause). Ids, audit stamps and dates are skipped and counted. An ambiguous legacy number is refused naming the ids; legacy=<number> picks it.

inputs.name: kind
inputs.description: The kind of record, e.g. "Order".

inputs.name: number
inputs.description: The Document No on the twin.

inputs.name: legacy
inputs.description: The Document No on legacy when it differs from the twin's.

calls.who: the twin and the legacy database

verbs.title: Make the 2Pack zip from a data-model workbook (old name of mis.pack)
verbs.description: Reads an ERP data-model workbook (one sheet per dictionary table: table, columns, reference lists, window, tabs, menu, process rows with class names only, plus a Plugin sheet) and writes the metadata-only 2Pack zip a legacy iDempiere applies. Written once per version: the same version with the same rows answers unchanged, the same version with different rows is refused (a released pack is immutable; bump the version). The answer gives the zip's path, its sha256, the rows per dictionary table and the process class names the pack points at. With java= the Java model classes of the tables the workbook creates are written too; the rules (document actions, process bodies) stay hand-written. A person runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms.

inputs.name: book
inputs.description: The workbook, a .xlsx path inside this tree or the working folder (no .. and no absolute path).

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: The pack version, x.y.z.

inputs.name: out
inputs.description: Folder to write META-INF/2Pack_<version>.zip under (default: the door's cache).

inputs.name: java
inputs.description: Folder to write the generated Java model classes under (optional).

inputs.name: package
inputs.description: Java package of those classes (default org.kernel.bim.model).

verbs.title: Put a data-model plugin on the legacy test instance and check it there (old name of legacy.plugin)
verbs.description: The whole route for a plugin on a real legacy iDempiere, one line: start the docker Postgres if it is not running, make the 2Pack from the workbook, refresh the local legacy test instance from the base seed with the plugin bundle installed, read every row of the workbook back from the test database, and run the in-server witness. Each step is its own line and the first line that is not ok stops it. The refresh installs the plugin bundle as committed, so the check says when the installed pack is not the one just made from the workbook. About three minutes. A person runs it; an AI's call is held as a claim until a person confirms.

inputs.name: book
inputs.description: The workbook, a .xlsx path inside this tree.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: The pack version, x.y.z.

returns.shape: the envelopes of its lines, in answer.lines; the last is legacy.witness's
